curriculum.title: Jesus, the Confession, and the Church

core.big_idea: The church belongs to Jesus and lives under His identity, authority, reconciliation, and discipline.

passages.reading_note: Read in immediate context; use age-appropriate portions without changing the claim.

claims.statement: Peter confesses Jesus as the Messiah, the Son of the living God, and Jesus says He will build His church.
Jesus gives a process for addressing sin and seeking reconciliation within the community, including witnesses and congregational involvement.
Taken together, these passages support the lesson’s big idea: The church belongs to Jesus and lives under His identity, authority, reconciliation, and discipline.

core.interpretation_skill: Observe text; reconstruct context; account for genre; distinguish text, synthesis, inference, and application

learning.extension_objective: Test the claim against context, genre, canonical synthesis, credible alternatives, and the limits of the available evidence.

theological_guardrails: Church discipline texts can be misused by abusive leaders. Reconciliation never requires concealing crime, tolerating abuse, or bypassing safeguarding/civil reporting duties. Distinguish Jesus’ authority from human leaders’ fallible judgments.
Questions and disagreement may be expressed without embarrassment or coercion.
